text: When substituting a term t for a free variable x in φ, if t contains a variable y that would fall within the scope of a ∀y or ∃y in φ, that occurrence of y becomes wrongly bound — the phenomenon called variable capture, which is avoided by α-renaming.
explanation: True. Variable capture occurs when a free variable of t is 'captured' by a quantifier in φ, altering the meaning; the standard remedy is to α-rename the offending bound variable before substituting. Proof assistants avoid capture automatically via de Bruijn indices.
